item.title: Know and Celebrate Your Purpose for the Positive Future of Humanity — Sun Oct 25, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Raleigh & Triangle Activities Meetup Group What do you need to live happy ever after? Assuming that you still believe a happy ending is still possible for you. So many people have given up, it’s sad. And dangerous. Giving up invites all manner of negativity with self-fulfilling prophecies of doom. When I was young I expected that world peace, global health, and personal love and wealth were waiting just ahead. Then the years and decades taught me otherwise. Like most folks I worked hard for my dreams in so many ways, picking myself up to try and try again. How can you not feel insecure and jealous when others luck into what’s out of reach for you? And of course, we all may fear and loathe the destructive fools who make every problem worse – even if we disagree on which fools are to blame. Now with the whole planet on the brink of disaster, it looks like we’ve all been fooled and we failed the game of life. Or have we?

item.title: Craft Club: Alcohol Ink Coasters — Mon Oct 26, 6:30 PM — The Glass Jug Downtown
item.description: Looking for something fun to do in Durham on a Monday night? Come create with us at our very first Craft Club with Durham Craft Company at The Glass Jug Beer Lab in downtown Durham! Join us and make your own set of unique coasters using vibrant colors at this fun class. We’re making alcohol ink coasters, and the best part? They’re practically foolproof! item.title: Beyond advice: Building effective mentor-mentee relationships — Tue Oct 27, 10:00 AM — None
item.description:
REGISTRATION: Click Here
NOTE: Please register ahead of the event.
Join us for the Duke Office of Scientific Integrity's Virtual Research Town Hall, "Beyond advice: Building effective mentor-mentee relationships" on October 27, 2026 from 10:00am - 11:30am.
Effective mentorship plays a critical role in research excellence, career development, and fostering a positive research culture within the research community. Our speakers will explore mentorship as a key component of researcher development, including how mentoring differs from other forms of professional support and how researchers can cultivate meaningful and productive mentoring relationships.
Attending this event fulfills the RCR-200 requirement for Faculty and Staff, the 200-level NSF RECR requirement, and the 754 RCR credit for graduate students. Participants must attend for at least 60 minutes to receive credit.
Source: Duke University

Discussion and an activity will offer participants space to investigate the possibilities and limitations for AI in their work.

item.description:

item.title: How Values Develop, Change, and Interact with Life — Tue Oct 27, 12:00 PM — None
item.description:
This webinar explores where values originate and how they develop over time. Participants will learn how values are influenced by social, culture, and life experiences, as well as how they emerge from our needs and broader societal influences. The webinar will explore how emotions, well-being, and experiences of uncertainty can influence the values people prioritize.

item.title: Learning in Networks Reading Group — Tue Oct 27, 12:00 PM — Gross Hall
item.description:
Learning in Networks Reading Group and Seminar Series: Tuesdays, 12pm in 330 Gross Hall; lunch included The institute focuses on fundamental questions in statistical inference, machine learning, causal inference, and optimization on networks, with particular emphasis on statistical-computational tradeoffs, message-passing algorithms, learning dynamics, and network-based market design. By fostering collaboration across disciplines, the institute aims to develop new mathematical and algorithmic foundations for understanding complex networked systems and their applications. The institute is led by collaborators Jiaming Xu, Alex Belloni, Fan Wei, Galen Reeves, and James Moody. Learn more: https://sites.duke.edu/learninginnetworks/
Source: Duke University

item.title: Live Music at Motorco: Friko with Nine Perfect Lives — Tue Oct 27, 8:00 PM — Motorco
item.description:
Friko will be partnering with Plus1 to collect funds for Santa for a Day! $1 from every ticket sold will go to Santa for a Day, a certified 501 (c) (3) Public Charity who answers letters to Santa from kids in underserved communities. This two-pronged literacy component is vital to their mission: Volunteers helping, teaching youngsters the power of the pen… and then donors rewarding their efforts, by translating their wishes into reality, This process helps children feel seen, heard, and valued—often for the first time—while fostering family dignity and empowerment that extends well beyond the holidays as participants author a different, more positive narrative about life, one sparked by optimism and the vision of a brighter future. Founded in 2018, SFAD has fulfilled more than 50,000 letters and delivered nearly 100,000 gifts to children across eight U.S. cities.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: OMFG! You Grew A Tail! — Wed Oct 28, 6:00 PM — Future Hooman
item.description: Congratulations! Your body has developed a tail. We have absolutely no idea how this happened. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll fabricate your very own fully functioning LED tail from scratch. We’ll provide the materials, tools, and questionable scientific supervision. You provide the willingness to grow something weird. No experience necessary. You’ll learn how to shape, sew and stuff your tail, then install the LED system and bring your new appendage to life. Your finished tail has multiple animated lighting modes, so you can switch up your glow depending on your mood, your outfit, or whatever mysterious creature you have decided to become. And yes, you get to take your new body modification home. Your new tail is perfect for your next Halloween costume, rave, or just being dramatically more interesting than anyone else. • Minimum age: 16. • No experience needed. • Approximate time: 1–1.5 hours. • 6 people per session. • $50 workshop fee + tax includes all materials and tools.

item.title: Dueling Dinosaurs Sensory Friendly Mornings — Sun Nov 8, 10:00 AM — Downtown Raleigh
item.description:
Explore the Dueling Dinosaurs exhibit with reduced noise effects and smaller crowds. Please bring any noise-reducing headphones and fidgets you may need! A limited number of Sensory Friendly Bags are available for checkout at the front desk, and a limited number of noise-reducing headphones are available to borrow at the exhibit. Free registration is not necessary but encouraged; if you register, we’ll send reminder emails and resources about the exhibit so you can know before you go! Please note that this is a self-guided tour of the exhibit space (not led by a museum educator), though you may interact with the research team in the SECU DinoLab! Register Now!
Recommended Audience All ages, particularly neurodivergent audiences. Children must be accompanied by adults.
Questions? If you have any questions, please contact the Coordinator of Accessibility, Sam Frigerio, at Accessibility@NaturalSciences.org or 919.707.9824.
Source: NC Museum of Natural Sciences

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Fri Jan 22 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.

item.title: Shia Islamic-Jewish Legal Reasoning in Dialogue — Sun Oct 25, 8:00 AM — Langford 152
item.description:
Over the last four years, the Shia Islamic-Jewish Legal Reasoning in Dialogue has brought together 13 scholars from across the U.S. and internationally to study legal texts of both traditions via diverse methodologies of academic analysis. They have been divided into 6 working groups working on the topics of the legal self, constitutionalism, theocracy, language, female clerical authority, and the persecution of heretics. The Dialogue is not merely meant to identify similarities and differences, but to allow scholars to think their "own" tradition conceptually anew through this encounter. The project arrives at Duke in order to present its findings and receive constructive critique from Triangle-area scholars of co-written book chapters that will eventually be published in Rutgers University Press' "Transmodern Times" series.
More information at: https://jewishstudies.duke.edu/shia-islamic-jewish-legal-reasoning-dialogue

item.title: CEE Seminar - Understanding and Computation of Deformation and Failure in Porous Microstructures — Mon Oct 26, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: This talk presents a body of work aimed at closing that gap, premised on the idea that a sharper physical understanding of how porous solids fail is what enables good approximations of it. Mechanical stress in a loaded microstructure concentrates at the geometric constrictions of the solid, which we hypothesize to be the preferred sites for cracks to nucleate under most loads. This is the basis for a reduced-order model that foreshadows where cracks form and thereby gains several orders of magnitude in computational speed. This hypothesis, which was first supported by phase-field simulations, is now being confirmed by in-situ tensile experiments on 3D-printed porous specimens. Underlying these approximations is a pore-level multiscale method (PLMM) that decomposes the solid into subdomains with local, physics-based closures.
